title: Short Stuff: Fear of Public Speaking
summary: Short Stuff episode on the fear of public speaking (glossophobia). The hosts open with banter about their own stage fright and how they overcame it through exposure. They cover the popular poll claim that public speaking ranks above death as a fear, and note glossophobia is a form of social anxiety disorder rooted in fear of judgment and failure, and the fear of the fear that drives avoidance. They describe physical symptoms, explain the amygdala and fight-or-flight response, discuss how fear may start in childhood and how parents should encourage kids without traumatizing them. They close with advice: start small, seek cognitive behavioral therapy if severe, join groups like Toastmasters, and know material well rather than memorizing it. A brief ad break for a sponsor appears mid-episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and stage fright
segments.summary: The hosts joke about their show changes and recall their own stage fright, noting they overcame it mostly through exposure. They introduce the topic of fear of public speaking.

segments.title: Prevalence, poll myth, and glossophobia
segments.summary: They question how common the fear is, mention the popular claim that public speaking beats death as the top American fear and the Jerry Seinfeld eulogy joke, and name the fear glossophobia. They note it is a legitimate social anxiety disorder.

segments.title: Fear of judgment and avoidance
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the core of social anxiety is fear of judgment and failure, that people fear the fear itself, and that avoidance is the main coping behavior, sometimes shaping careers and lives.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Short break before returning to the discussion, with a teaser from the hosts.

segments.title: Physical symptoms and the amygdala
segments.summary: They describe physical symptoms such as racing heart, sweating, trembling, dizziness and sleeplessness, then explain that the amygdala associates performance with fear and triggers a fight-or-flight stress response, possibly starting in childhood.

segments.title: Parenting and encouraging kids
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how parents can help children face fears without forcing them or traumatizing them, using a roller coaster anecdote as an example of the older, harsher approach.

segments.title: Treatment, practice tips, and sign-off
segments.summary: They recommend starting small, seeking cognitive behavioral therapy for severe cases, and progressing through practice audiences and Toastmasters. They advise knowing material rather than memorizing it, then sign off.
